element_string.guard: string pointer equal to element+0x10 skips the delete

assumptions: Field labels (holder offsets, element size, string layout) describe observed pointer arithmetic only, not confirmed source-level types.
Sized-delete sizes are the second argument observed at each PLT call site.
The string guard reading (pointer equal to element+0x10 means no heap allocation to free) is the observed branch condition; its source-level meaning is an inference, not a pinned fact.
The array range is treated as well-formed; a corrupt range or cyclic structure is not modelled.
behavior: Nested array teardown that frees its own inner holder: load inner = [holder]; a null inner returns plainly with nothing freed. Otherwise walk the inner vector triple [begin, end) of 8-byte pointers; per element, skip null pointers, else dispose the element string first when its pointer differs from element+0x10 (sized delete of capacity + 1, capacity at element+0x10), then free the element struct with a sized delete of 0x20, both through the _ZdlPvm PLT at 0x63f0d80. Reload begin from inner+0x00; when non-null free the array buffer with a sized delete of (capacity end - begin) bytes, capacity end from inner+0x10. Finally tail-jump to the sized-delete PLT freeing the inner object itself at 0x18. The outer holder in rdi is never freed, and no canary check is performed.

buffer_phase.null_begin: skips the buffer free, inner free still runs

consumers.note: Reached only by code, never by data. See callers.tsv for the site list.

exits.target: sized-delete PLT 0x63f0d80 freeing the inner object at 0x18
